overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by circulating a draft letter by email to the full Board before a meeting; the Committee violated it only by failing to timely respond to a complaint, and was found not to have violated it on the letter or the withheld minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board and School Committee deliberated outside a meeting to draft a letter to the Planning Board about the Mindess School Building Project.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that at no point did a quorum of the Committee communicate regarding the letter to the Planning Board.

allegations.summary: The Board's chair emailed a draft letter to the full Board before a meeting, and the letter contained the chair's opinions, so the distribution was deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the draft letter necessarily contained the opinions of Chair Magnani and should not have been distributed to the full Board outside of a properly noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee failed to respond to the first Open Meeting Law complaint within the required time.
allegations.key_passage: We find, and the Committee acknowledges in its November 3 response, that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely respond to the first complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee wrongly kept withholding minutes of an executive session discussing the first complaint after it had responded to that complaint.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the purpose for the October 21 executive session has not yet expired, and the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by continuing to withhold the executive session minutes.

remedy: Board: immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
Board: release to the public, within 30 days of the letter, the chair's August 18 email circulating the draft letter (if not already done).
remedy_passage: we order the Board, if it has not done so already, to release to the public within 30 days of the date of this letter Chair Magnani’s August 18 email circulating the draft letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
